{#vry1} # Background

{#dvbb} Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for roughly 85% of all lung cancer cases and substantially contributes to cancer deaths worldwide . Both immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) immunotherapy and radiotherapy are first-line treatments for NSCLC. For locally advanced NSCLC, chemoradiation combined with ICB has become the standard treatment. [@w:w1] However, the curative efficacy of radio-immunotherapy is still suboptimal, and radioresistance remains a significant barrier to improving the antitumor-immunity of IR, limiting the survival benefit of NSCLC from radiotherapy–immunotherapy combinations [@w:w2]. Therefore, there is an urgent need to investigate prospective combination modalities to enhance the antitumor immunity of IR.

{#ij16} Radiotherapy can elicit significant immunostimulatory effects, including triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD) and improving the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) [@w:w3]. However, there needs to be more strategies that could effectively boost the antitumor-immunity of radiotherapy in clinical settings due to inadequately elucidated mechanisms. The prevailing view suggests that radiation directly induces DNA damage and micronucleus formation in tumor cells, leading to DNA single- and double-strand breaks (DSBs) [@w:w4].
